Class GeneratedTypeHierarchy

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.core.type.GeneratedTypeHierarchy
All Implemented Interfaces:
TypeHierarchy
@Internal public non-sealed class GeneratedTypeHierarchy extends Object implements TypeHierarchy
The TypeHierarchy a generated record extends: a class with a single constructor, which the record calls with the type, its variables, its direct super types and all its super types built as Arguments from constants, so that a record is as small as that one call. It is public and not final because the records, generated into the packages of the application, extend it: TypeHierarchy is sealed to it, so this class and its subclasses are the only implementations.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

      protected GeneratedTypeHierarchy(Class<?> type, Argument<?> @Nullable [] typeVariables, @Nullable Argument<?> superclass, Argument<?> @Nullable [] interfaces, Argument<?> @Nullable [] superTypes)
      The constructor of the records written before the names of the super types a record leaves out were recorded. Such a record could have left super types out as well: its empty list of them means that it carries no information on what it left out, not that it left nothing out.
      Parameters:
      type - The type
      typeVariables - The type variables, or null for none
      superclass - The generic superclass, or null for none
      interfaces - The generic interfaces, or null for none
      superTypes - All the super types, Object last, or null for Object alone

      The super types of the type, transitively, with their type arguments written in the type variables of the type along the path that reaches them: the super class and its super types first, then each interface and its super types, each type once, Object last.     • getOmittedSuperTypeNames

      public final List<String> getOmittedSuperTypeNames()
      Description copied from interface: TypeHierarchy
      The names of the super types left out of the super types because the record could not name their declaration: one whose class is not public and of another package than the record, such as the package-private java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder of StringBuilder, or a public one whose type arguments name such a class at any depth, such as Supplier<List<Hidden>>. Each is the name of the class of the super type, without its type arguments, in the order of the super types and once, so that a consumer that knows the class by name, in its own package, can still tell it is a super type of the type.

      The names are erased evidence of membership only, not generic metadata: a super type Base<String> and a super type Base<Integer> are both p.Base, and nothing says what the type arguments of the super type left out were. A consumer that needs them reads them from a record of its own, written in the package of the class. A type variable bounded by such a class is not widened: leaving the bound out would change what the variable is bounded by and erases to, so a type whose variables are bounded by a class the record cannot name is not recorded from another package.

      A record written by a processor that predates this list, with the constructor of GeneratedTypeHierarchy that takes no names, has an empty list too: for such a record it carries no information on what was left out.

      Specified by:
      getOmittedSuperTypeNames in interface TypeHierarchy
      Returns:
      The names of the super types left out, empty when the record names them all or was written without them
